description: NASA researchers and collaborators publish this inventory of rainfall-triggered landslides in 22 Lower Mekong locations. They mapped initiation points from Planet imagery using a semi-automatic method, with two inventories in Laos, four in Myanmar, one in Thailand and fifteen in Vietnam. The Figshare page offers a 431 kB ZIP; the describing paper identifies a shapefile of landslide initiation points, imagery footprints and metadata. Figshare gives CC BY 4.0 and public access without charge. The geographic coverage spans those four Lower Mekong countries. In simulation, the points can train a rainfall-landslide hazard model or test exposure of roads and settlements during monsoon events. They are not polygon footprints or a complete count of every landslide. The paper reports that the method underestimated landslide area by 16.86 percent against a manual inventory and that image time gaps allowed vegetation recovery. Road-disruption use is a modeller inference, not an outcome measured in the dataset. No archive was opened or point geometry checked. The current catalogue has other hazard data, but no direct Lower Mekong initiation-point counterpart was identified.
name: Rainfall-induced landslide inventories for Lower Mekong
